text:
Vegas dominated the numbers and lost anyway. VGK outattempted ANA 66 to 47 and carried the better of the simulated replays, winning 59 percent of them, but the game was effectively settled in a nine-minute stretch of the second period. Alex Killorn tipped one in at 1:33, Jeff Malott deflected another 55 seconds later, and Leo Carlsson snapped a 27 percent chance past Carter Hart at 7:03 to make it 4-0. ANA had already led on Beckett Sennecke's wrist shot at 19:52 of the first.

That second period was the one stretch ANA controlled, 1.38 to 0.86 in expected goals. Hart allowed 1.3 goals more than the 20 shots against him deserved, and it showed. Carlsson finished with a goal and an assist, and Lukas Dostal made 27 saves on 30 shots, just ahead of what the chances against him warranted.

The third period belonged to VGK, who out-chanced ANA 1.57 to 0.81. Shea Theodore scored on a 6 percent look at 4:38, Tomas Hertl converted on the power play at 6:07, and Braeden Bowman made it 4-3 at 17:10. Hertl put five shots on goal and finished with 0.95 expected goals of his own. It wasn't enough to erase the early hole, and ANA hung on for the 4-3 win.
